My reasoning:

I have been doing stevia for some years now. My land is only 1.1 mu, so everything I do is on a small scale, but I still need to spend carefully because the seedlings alone cost me real money — maybe 400-500 yuan just for the seedlings from the dealer in town.

Last year I used one bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg, the 15-15-15 kind) as base before transplanting. That worked okay so I will do the same again. Then I top-dress with urea two times — about half a bag (25 kg) split across the season, once after the plants take root and once before the first cutting. The dealer told me stevia likes potassium for the leaves, so I also add maybe 10 kg of potassium sulfate when I side-dress. My neighbors who also grow stevia do similar.

I use improved seedlings from the contract company — they give us the type, we cannot really choose. I transplant by hand with my wife and son when he is home.

For water, I have a well, so I irrigate after transplanting to help roots take, then 3-4 more times during dry spells in summer. Quzhou summer can be hot and dry.

Pesticide — stevia gets some aphids and sometimes leaf spot. I spray maybe 3 times total, once early, once mid-season, once before cutting. I do not want to spray too much because the buyer checks.

I plough once with the small tractor before transplanting, then use rotary to make it fine. For yield, last year I got about 350 kg dry leaf per mu. I hope for similar this year.
